answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can tie influence to earned, decaying work credits rather than headcount. Each agent starts with almost nothing and gains standing only by completing verified tasks whose outputs peers can check, like tending a shared garden where only real cultivation yields nectar. Credits fade over time, so old identities cannot rest on past glory, and a stake is slashed for fraud. Crossing the canyon from newcomer to trusted participant therefore costs sustained effort, making fake armies expensive while honest agents keep their standing by continuing useful work.
